summary: Defines three YANG data models for Segment Routing: one for configuration and operation, which different data planes augment, one with generic types and groupings, and one for the Segment Routing MPLS data plane.

plainLanguage.summary: Standard settings forms for a routing method where packets carry their own route, so tools can configure it uniformly.

questions: what is the yang model for segment routing
what is srgb in segment routing
subtitle: Standard YANG data models so routers can configure and monitor Segment Routing the same way.

tldr.problem: Segment Routing needs to be configured and monitored on routers from different vendors, and without a common data model each one would be managed differently.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC defines three YANG modules: a generic one that hooks into the routing model, a common one with shared types and groupings, and one for the SR MPLS data plane.
tldr.outcome: Operators can use NETCONF or RESTCONF to configure SIDs, label blocks and Adj-SID properties, read the SID database, and receive notifications about collisions.

facts.label: Notification throttle
facts.value: At least 5 seconds apart (SID collision, index out of range)

today: RFC 9020 is a Proposed Standard published in May 2021. The metadata lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Three Modules for Segment Routing
sections.content:
RFC 9020 defines three YANG data models for Segment Routing (SR), the architecture of RFC 8402. The first is for SR configuration and operation. The second holds generic types and groupings that other modules can reuse. The third configures and operates the SR MPLS data plane described in RFC 8660.

The RFC does not define the IGP extensions for SR. Instead, the common module offers groupings that IGP extension modules can reuse. The stated reason is that implementations should not be forced to support every IGP extension: a device may support the IS-IS extension but not the OSPF one. All the modules conform to the Network Management Datastore Architecture (NMDA) of RFC 8342.
sections.plainLanguage: There are three forms: one general form, one with shared building blocks, and one specific to a certain kind of road system. You only fill in the ones your router needs.

sections.title: How the Modules Fit Together
sections.content:
The ietf-segment-routing module augments the routing container of the routing model in RFC 8349 and defines generic SR configuration and operational state. By itself it only adds an empty segment-routing container, which modules for different data planes are meant to augment.

ietf-segment-routing-mpls augments that container and supports the SR-MPLS data plane. ietf-segment-routing-common defines generic types and groupings that SHOULD be reused by IGP extension modules.
sections.plainLanguage: The general module is an empty shelf. The MPLS module puts its own boxes on that shelf, and the common module is a drawer of parts that both can borrow.

sections.title: Global Configuration
sections.content:
The sr-mpls container holds all configuration for the SR MPLS data plane, split into global and interface configuration. Global configuration has four parts.

  • Bindings map prefixes to Segment Identifiers (Prefix-SIDs). A mapping server maps prefixes that are not local to a SID, and several mapping policies may be defined. Connected prefixes map local prefixes to a SID, given as an index (the default) or an absolute value. Configuring a binding does not by itself allow it to be advertised: each routing-protocol instance controls that.
  • last-hop-behavior sets MPLS Penultimate Hop Popping behavior to explicit-null, php or non-php.
  • The SRGB (Segment Routing Global Block) is a list of label blocks, each a lower-bound and upper-bound pair. It is agnostic to the control plane, so all local routing-protocol instances must advertise the same SRGB.
  • The SRLB (Segment Routing Local Block) is a similar list of label blocks reserved for local SIDs.
sections.plainLanguage: You tell the router which numbers stand for which destinations, and which range of numbers it may use. Some numbers are shared by everyone, and some are kept for private use.

sections.title: IGP Configuration and Adjacency SIDs
sections.content:
SR support for a particular IGP is added by augmenting that routing protocol's configuration. This augmentation SHOULD live in the routing-protocol YANG modules, so nobody has to support SR for every protocol. The sr-control-plane grouping has an enabled leaf to turn on SR extensions for a protocol instance, and a bindings container that controls advertising local bindings and processing received ones.

Interface configuration is part of the igp-interface grouping and covers Adjacency SID (Adj-SID) properties. For parallel links between two routers, advertise-adj-group-sid lists group IDs, and interfaces with the same group ID are bundled behind one extra Adj-SID. The RFC's example has four links, L1 to L4, grouped as L1/L2 and L3/L4, giving Adj-SID values of 400 and 500.

advertise-protection sets how protection is advertised and does not turn protection on or off. With single, one Adj-SID is advertised and the B-Flag is set if the interface is protected. With dual, a protected interface gets two Adj-SIDs, one with the B-Flag set and one with it clear, for traffic engineering paths that must use either protected or unprotected segments.
sections.plainLanguage: If two roads join the same towns, you can give both together one nickname. You can also say whether a road has a spare route ready in case it breaks.

sections.title: State Data and Notifications
sections.content:
Operational state shows how the allocated SRGB labels are used. The label-blocks list reports each block's bounds, size, free and used counts and scope (global or local). The sid-db lists all global SIDs with their bindings, source protocol, algorithm and whether the binding is installed in the forwarding plane.

Three notifications are defined:

  • segment-routing-srgb-collision is raised when control-plane-advertised SRGB blocks conflict.
  • segment-routing-global-sid-collision is raised when an advertised index is already tied to another target.
  • segment-routing-index-out-of-range is raised when an advertised index falls outside the SRGBs configured on the device.

In the module text, the last two notifications must be throttled with at least a 5-second gap between them.
sections.plainLanguage: The router keeps a notebook of which numbers are in use and rings a bell when two people claim the same number or use one outside the allowed range.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content:
The modules are accessed through NETCONF or RESTCONF, whose mandatory-to-implement secure transports are SSH and TLS. The Network Configuration Access Control Model (NACM) can limit which users may reach which nodes.

Writable nodes can hurt if unprotected. Changing the local bindings could cause a denial-of-service (DoS) attack, and an attacker might create segment conflicts, using one identifier for different purposes, to redirect traffic inside the trusted domain, for example towards compromised nodes or around a firewall. Shrinking the SRGB to a very small size could stop many existing segments from being installed. The SRLB is open to similar attacks.

Reading is sensitive too. Knowledge of the bindings can help attack the local router, and the sid-db can be used to attack other routers in the SR domain or to redirect traffic meant for them.
sections.plainLanguage: If a stranger could change the router's number list, they could send traffic to the wrong place or break it. So only trusted people should be allowed to read or change these settings.

sections.title: Configuration Examples
sections.content: The appendix gives IPv4 and IPv6 examples in both XML and JSON. In the IPv4 example, a mapping-server policy named mapping 1 maps the prefix 198.51.100.0/24 with start-sid 200 and range 100. A connected prefix 192.0.2.0/24 gets start-sid 100, range 1 and last-hop-behavior php. The SRGB runs from 45000 to 55000. The IPv6 example has the same shape, using the prefixes 2001:db8:aaaa:bbbb::/64 and 2001:db8:aaaa:cccc::/64.
sections.plainLanguage: The examples are filled-in sample forms that show what a finished configuration looks like.
